_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); hotel signals

pit_profile.why: Marriott: 'Consistent with our focus on management, franchising, and licensing, we own very few of our lodging properties'; 'We operate, franchise, or license 4,424 properties worldwide, with 759,330 rooms as of year-end 2015'; 'Our industry is highly competitive, which may impact our ability to compete successfully with other hotel properties and home and apartment sharing services for customers'; 'Economic uncertainty could continue to impact our financial results and growth'; 'An increase in the use of third-party Internet services to book online hotel reservations could adversely impact our business'; 'Our 2015 results reflected a favorable economic climate and demand for our brands in many markets around the world, reflecting generally low supply growth in the U.S. and Europe, moderate GDP growth in North America, improved pricing in most North American markets, and a year-over-year increase in the number of properties in our system'; and, of the pending merger, 'On November 15, 2015, we entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the “Merger Agreement”) to combine with Starwood Hotels & Resorts Worldwide, Inc.' and 'We currently estimate that, upon completion of the combination, our shareholders before the merger will own approximately 61% and former Starwood shareholders will own approximately 39% of the combined company’s outstanding common stock' (its own FY2015 10-K): a hotel management and franchise system whose fees follow the revenues and profits of its hotels through the economy, by its own account; no disruption theme is live for it

classification.quality_note: Marriott: 'Consistent with our focus on management, franchising, and licensing, we own very few of our lodging properties'; 'We operate, franchise, or license 4,424 properties worldwide, with 759,330 rooms as of year-end 2015'; 'Our industry is highly competitive, which may impact our ability to compete successfully with other hotel properties and home and apartment sharing services for customers'; 'Economic uncertainty could continue to impact our financial results and growth'; 'An increase in the use of third-party Internet services to book online hotel reservations could adversely impact our business'; 'Our 2015 results reflected a favorable economic climate and demand for our brands in many markets around the world, reflecting generally low supply growth in the U.S. and Europe, moderate GDP growth in North America, improved pricing in most North American markets, and a year-over-year increase in the number of properties in our system'; and, of the pending merger, 'On November 15, 2015, we entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the “Merger Agreement”) to combine with Starwood Hotels & Resorts Worldwide, Inc.' and 'We currently estimate that, upon completion of the combination, our shareholders before the merger will own approximately 61% and former Starwood shareholders will own approximately 39% of the combined company’s outstanding common stock' (its own FY2015 10-K): a hotel management and franchise system whose fees follow the revenues and profits of its hotels through the economy, by its own account; no disruption theme is live for it. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.72x; -2% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +0.79; conservative 2yr +56%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -37.6%/yr (worst year FY06-FY15, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +10.3%/yr (Q1 fee guide + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +10.3%/yr (FY06-FY15 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +26.8%/yr (best 2-yr run FY06-FY15); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: MAR (retrospective, 2016-04-08) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.72x (57.9% downside to Bear $28 / +80.3% upside to Bull $120) | Adj composite 2.59 vs market 1.80: gap +0.79 [UNDERVALUED] | -2% above the EPP floor $68 (18x FY16E $3.77) | Conservative 2-yr case: +56.1% total (+28.1%/yr) | At 17.6x FY16E the 15% hurdle price $88 sits at or below the BASE case; North American RevPAR +4.6% in Q4 2015, forward fee revenue +4-6% (Q1 2016 fee revenue guide); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
